title: English Colonial Empire
capsule: The English Colonial Empire, spanning roughly 1607 to 1707 before it was recast as the British Empire under the Acts of Union, originated with the Jamestown settlement (1607) and the Bermuda charter (1609) and expanded through conquest, charter, and proprietary grant across North America, the Caribbean, and coastal India. Its Atlantic economy was structured around plantation agriculture and the slave trade: the Royal African Company, chartered 1660, initially monopolized the supply of enslaved Africans to English colonies. The seizure of Jamaica from Spain (1655) and New Netherland from the Dutch (1664) were strategic turning points. The Glorious Revolution of 1688 and subsequent parliamentary supremacy over colonial governance shaped the constitutional framework that the Thirteen Colonies would later contest.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The territorial footprint is well documented through colonial charters and surveys; the map polygons represent claimed or administered territories and omit large interior regions under indigenous control that lie outside English administrative reach.
